runs.text: 1. Leverage is falling but high. Consolidated principal debt of USD 20,168 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 20,232 million at December 31, 2025) over derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,918 million gives 5.15x gross and 4.51x net, against 6.18x and 5.78x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Debt barely moved, so the improvement comes from earnings and from cash rising to USD 2,485 million. [Documentary Fact for the inputs; the ratio is a derived Analyst Interpretation, not a covenant measure.] 2. The parent group deleveraged in Q3 2026. Bausch Health (excl. B+L) net debt fell from USD 13,651 million to USD 13,130 million, a reduction of USD 521 million in the quarter, while its debt was USD 15,103 million [CP-1]. Bausch + Lomb debt was USD 5,065 million and its cash and revolver are generally not available to the parent [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the net debt figures are derived.] 3. Liquidity is adequate near term but thinner at the parent. Consolidated cash plus undrawn revolvers was USD 3,620 million; the parent's share was USD 2,442 million (cash USD 1,973 million including restricted cash, plus USD 469 million undrawn) [CP-1]. The USD 643 million 2027 notes will be redeemed from cash on November 30, 2026, which reduces parent liquidity to about USD 1,799 million pro forma [CP-1, calculation below]. [Analyst Interpretation.] 4. The maturity wall starts in 2028. Debt maturing is USD 15 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 701 million in 2027, USD 3,766 million in 2028, USD 1,667 million in 2029, USD 4,123 million in 2030 and USD 3,896 million in 2031, with USD 6,000 million thereafter [CP-1]. The parent's 2028 maturities of USD 2,326 million exceed its pro forma liquidity of about USD 1,799 million, so repayment relies on cash generation or refinancing; the revolver also has an earlier-maturity trigger tied to indebtedness above USD 1,000 million [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Analyst Interpretation.] 5. Earnings quality is price-led and concentrated. Salix revenue rose USD 343 million in nine months 2026 on price of USD 504 million, partly offset by volumes down USD 173 million, and Salix is about 27% of revenue but about 47% of segment profit [CP-1A]. Xifaxan is about 85% of Salix, faces a negotiated Medicare price from January 1, 2027 and expected generics in 2028, and the company impaired Salix goodwill by USD 1,426 million in January 2026 after failed Phase 3 trials [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the concentration shares are derived.] 6. Cash interest absorbs a large share of earnings. FY2025 cash interest was USD 1,810 million against derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,276 million, about 55% of it and a cover of 1.81x, and the pack gives no interim cash interest [CP-1]. Premium accounting makes P&L interest lower than cash interest, so cover on a P&L basis (2.53x LTM Q3 2026) is flattered [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact for inputs; Analyst Interpretation on direction.] 7. Structure matters as much as leverage. The 2025 first-lien debt at 126NumberCo holds a lien on 211,963,893 Bausch + Lomb shares, and sales proceeds must prepay it pro rata with the 2032 notes; other secured and unsecured notes rank structurally behind, and Bausch + Lomb's earnings and net debt are outside the covenant [CP-1A]. Legal capacity and exchange terms cannot be tested without the debt documents. [Documentary Fact.] 8. Governance evidence is mixed rather than adverse. No dividends and a USD 50 million buyback authorised, a cash repurchase of near-par unsecured notes in 2025 and extended maturities weigh against overlapping leadership of two listed entities and unresolved terms of exchanges [CP-1A]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

runs.text: - Earnings recovery with deleveraging. Derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments rose from USD 3,276 million (FY2025) to USD 3,918 million (LTM Q3 2026) while principal debt stayed near USD 20,200 million, lowering gross leverage by about one turn [CP-1]. This reduces default risk on a going-concern basis. [Analyst Interpretation.] - Refinancing already done. The 2025 refinancing and the December 2025 exchange extended about USD 6,870 million and USD 1,600 million of maturities to 2030 through 2032, so only USD 716 million falls due before 2028 on a consolidated basis, and USD 643 million of that is to be redeemed from cash [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact for the transactions; the 716 sum is derived.] - Cash and parent deleveraging. Cash of USD 2,485 million and parent net debt down USD 521 million in Q3 2026 show cash generation reaching the parent group [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact.] - Covenant exposure is limited and stated compliant. The revolver has two maintenance tests, and the company states compliance at September 30, 2026 [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact; the headroom is Not supplied.] - Diversification outside Salix. International, Solta Medical and Bausch + Lomb grew in nine months 2026, and Bausch + Lomb produced about 27% of segment profit [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the share is derived.] - No shareholder leakage. No dividends in FY2025, FY2024 or FY2023, and restrictions in the debt documents [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact.]

- Product concentration with dated erosion. Salix and Xifaxan dominate segment profit, and the negotiated price and generic entry are dated [CP-1A]. Mechanic: price-led growth meets a price cap, then volume loss. Implication: lower cash available for 2028 refinancing. [Documentary Fact for the dates; Analyst Interpretation on the effect.] - High leverage and modest cash cover. 5.15x gross leverage and 1.81x FY2025 cash interest cover leave limited tolerance for a profit decline [CP-1]. [Analyst Interpretation.] - Large 2028 to 2031 maturities, USD 13,452 million in total, with USD 8,422 million of it at the parent [CP-1, calculation below]. [Analyst Interpretation.] - Structural subordination and a separate Bausch + Lomb silo. Value in the Bausch + Lomb stake serves the 2025 first-lien debt first, and its cash is generally trapped [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact.] - Weak credit ratings: Moody's Caa2 and S&P B- corporate, with a negative outlook at S&P and Rating Watch Evolving at Fitch [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact.] - Litigation and regulatory exposure: antitrust class actions on the Xifaxan settlement, a Luxembourg tax assessment with no reserve, an FDA warning letter at a Bausch + Lomb plant, and talc claims backed by an indemnity from Johnson & Johnson whose performance the pack does not test [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; amounts of exposure are Not supplied.] - Opaque adjusted measures. Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted cash flow are management-defined, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is missing, so no adjusted LTM leverage exists [CP-0, CP-1]. [Insufficient Information.]

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition or leveraged buyout is pending at the issuer; the transactions that matter are financing and structural, and all are described from filings, not from the executed documents, which are not supplied.

The 2022 Exchange closed on September 30, 2022: validly tendered senior unsecured notes of 5,594 were exchanged for 3,125 of new secured notes, a reduction of principal of 2,469, and the company concluded it met the criteria for a troubled debt restructuring under ASC 470-60 (Q3 10-Q page:40). On November 29, 2022 the company designated 126NumberCo, which holds Bausch + Lomb, as an unrestricted subsidiary, so Bausch + Lomb and its subsidiaries are outside the covenants of the Bausch Health debt documents (page:39, page:40). In March 2025, in connection with the April 2025 refinancing, 126NumberCo was re-designated a restricted subsidiary while Bausch + Lomb and its subsidiaries remained unrestricted (page:40).

The April 2025 Refinancing Transactions closed on April 8, 2025: 126NumberCo entered the 2025 Credit Agreement (a 500 five-year revolving credit facility due April 8, 2030 and a 3,000 term loan B due October 8, 2030) and issued 4,400 of 10.00% senior secured notes due April 15, 2032. Proceeds repaid or redeemed 6,870 of principal in total (the February 2027 term loan B of 2,156 and certain notes), which the company says extended approximately 6,870 of maturities from 2025 through 2028 to 2030 through 2032 (page:29, page:82, page:83). In August 2025 the company repurchased and retired 9.25% senior unsecured notes of about 602 par for about 601 of cash on hand (page:40). In December 2025 the company and 126NumberCo exchanged 797 of 4.875% senior secured notes due 2028 and 886 of 11.00% first lien notes due 2028 for 1,600 of new 10.00% senior secured notes due April 2032, which form one series with the earlier 2032 notes, reducing outstanding principal by 83; 26,495,472 Bausch + Lomb shares were transferred to 126NumberCo as part of the transaction and the exchange was accounted for as a modification, not a troubled debt restructuring (page:30, page:83, page:84).

At Bausch + Lomb, the June 2025 refinancing added an 800 revolving credit facility due June 26, 2030, a 2,325 term loan B due January 15, 2031 and EUR 675 floating rate notes due January 2031; in January 2026 a new 2,802 term loan facility due January 15, 2031 refinanced the 2028 and 2031 term loans in full (page:35, page:36, page:84). No new bond issue by the parent is described for 2026 in the pages read; nine months 2026 issuance of long-term debt of 2,930 is described as primarily the 2,802 of Bausch + Lomb refinancing proceeds and 75 of revolver borrowings (page:126).

After the quarter, the company announced on October 28, 2026 that its subsidiary Bausch Health Americas, Inc. will issue an irrevocable redemption notice on October 29, 2026 for all of its 8.500% senior notes due 2027, about 643 of principal, with redemption scheduled for November 30, 2026 and funded from cash on hand (page:76). This is a subsequent event and is not in any September 30, 2026 balance. The board also authorised a share repurchase of up to 50 on October 24, 2026, aimed at offsetting dilution from 2027 management equity vesting per the release (page:76; Q3 release page:1). Bausch + Lomb agreed on October 8, 2026 to buy ophthalmic surgical manufacturing businesses for about 85 upfront, due at closing in the fourth quarter of 2026 (page:18).

Other transactions affecting business risk: the December 2025 acquisition of the aesthetics distribution business of Solta's China distributor for about 87 aggregate consideration (page:15); the September 2025 DURECT acquisition for 84 with potential sales-based milestones of up to 350 (page:17); and a December 2025 Bausch + Lomb purchase of manufacturing equipment for about 75 upfront with up to 35 of milestones (page:17).

fields.value: The business is a specialty pharmaceutical and medical device group that sells about 60% of its revenue in the U.S. (FY2025, 10-K page:29) and holds about 87% of Bausch + Lomb, an eye health company that generates nearly half of consolidated revenue (4,013 of 8,317 for nine months 2026, Q3 10-Q page:75). The company states that generic Xifaxan is expected in 2028 and that a negotiated Medicare price takes effect on January 1, 2027 (page:96, page:98), and that Salix reporting unit goodwill was impaired by 1,426 after two Phase 3 trials of a new formulation failed in January 2026 (page:26).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction history that matters to creditors is structural. Since 2022 the company has moved Bausch + Lomb shares into a holding company, 126NumberCo, and in 2025 used those shares as collateral for new first-lien debt that extended maturities from 2025 through 2028 to 2030 through 2032 (page:82, page:83). The Existing Senior Secured Notes are structurally subordinated to liabilities of 126NumberCo and to debt secured by assets outside their collateral such as the Bausch + Lomb share collateral (page:39), and the Senior Unsecured Notes are not guaranteed by 126NumberCo or 153NumberCo (page:130). Bausch + Lomb's earnings and net debt are excluded from the parent's financial maintenance covenant (page:40). Creditors therefore hold a claim on a group whose most valuable subsidiary sits in a separate credit silo, and the company has described a full separation of Bausch + Lomb as subject to targeted leverage ratios and approvals (page:10). Net proceeds from any sale of the pledged shares must be applied to prepay the 2025 term loan and the 2032 notes pro rata (page:33, page:38).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Recent operating momentum is real but price-led, and the legal and regulatory calendar is dense. The main uncertainties for monitoring are the Xifaxan price and generic timeline, the Bausch + Lomb separation path, refinancing of the 2028 to 2031 maturities, and the unsupplied debt documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability and concentration. Evidence: Salix is about 27% of revenue and about 47% of segment profit, Xifaxan is about 85% of Salix, growth was price-led (price 504, volumes down 173), a negotiated price starts January 1, 2027 and generic entry is expected in 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:75, page:123, page:96, page:98). Risk mechanic: the product that earns the largest share of segment profit faces a price reset and then volume erosion just as 2028 maturities of 3,766 become due (CP-1). Credit implication: refinancing capacity in 2028 depends on how much Xifaxan cash flow remains, which makes monitoring of Xifaxan sales, the 2027 price effect and the generic timeline a leading indicator for refinancing risk. Counter-evidence: Salix profit rose 28% in nine months 2026 and management raised guidance; neither tests the post-2027 level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Structural subordination and the Bausch + Lomb silo. Evidence: first-lien claims at 126NumberCo hold the pledged Bausch + Lomb shares, and other secured and unsecured notes rank structurally behind (page:31, page:39); Bausch + Lomb's net debt and earnings are outside the covenant perimeter (page:40). Risk mechanic: value from the Bausch + Lomb stake flows first to the 2025 term loan and 2032 notes through the sweep (page:33, page:38). Credit implication: recovery prospects for notes outside that structure depend on residual value in the shares and on Bausch Health (excl. B+L) assets, with no expected recovery stated here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments rose to 3,918 on an LTM basis, while FY2025 cash interest cover was 1.81x on interest paid of 1,810 (CP-1). Risk mechanic: high cash interest and premium accounting mean P&L interest understates cash cost. Credit implication: cover is modest on a cash basis, so a decline in Salix profit would reduce cover quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Sponsor and governance alignment. Evidence: no dividends and a small buyback, an issuer-level pattern of maturity extension, but unresolved participation terms in exchanges and overlapping leadership of two listed entities (page:127, page:76, page:138). Credit implication: mixed; the pack neither shows leakage nor tests the indentures' restrictions.

fields.value: This module synthesises the fundamental credit view of Bausch Health Companies Inc. (issuer id `bhc`) as of 2026-11-05, for the credit_snapshot pathway, from the CP-1 financial base and the CP-1A business and transaction context. It uses upstream handoffs only and adds no new source reading; it gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion. Amounts are USD millions as reported by the issuer, and periods are labelled Q3 2026, nine months 2026, FY2025 and LTM Q3 2026.

fields.value: Consistency with the handoffs: the CP-1 correction to CP-0 on the Bausch + Lomb note issuers stands. This module repeats CP-1 and CP-1A figures without change and recomputes only the sums shown in `## Calculations`.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bausch Health is a highly leveraged, structurally complex credit that is improving but not yet resilient. Its strongest support is liquidity and momentum: USD 2,485 million of consolidated cash and USD 1,135 million of undrawn revolvers at September 30, 2026, derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,918 million, and debt to that EBITDA down from 6.18x to 5.15x [CP-1]. Its weakest point is dependence on Salix and Xifaxan, about 47% of segment profit, which faces a negotiated Medicare price from 2027 and expected generics in 2028, just before USD 3,766 million of debt falls due in 2028 [CP-1A, CP-1]. The outcome turns on how much Xifaxan cash flow survives 2027, and on whether USD 13,452 million due in 2028 to 2031 is refinanced inside a structure that ranks Bausch + Lomb value to the 2025 first-lien debt first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Leverage is falling but high. Consolidated principal debt of USD 20,168 million at September 30, 2026 (USD 20,232 million at December 31, 2025) over derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,918 million gives 5.15x gross and 4.51x net, against 6.18x and 5.78x at FY2025 [CP-1]. Debt barely moved, so the improvement comes from earnings and from cash rising to USD 2,485 million. [Documentary Fact for the inputs; the ratio is a derived Analyst Interpretation, not a covenant measure.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. The parent group deleveraged in Q3 2026. Bausch Health (excl. B+L) net debt fell from USD 13,651 million to USD 13,130 million, a reduction of USD 521 million in the quarter, while its debt was USD 15,103 million [CP-1]. Bausch + Lomb debt was USD 5,065 million and its cash and revolver are generally not available to the parent [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the net debt figures are derived.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Liquidity is adequate near term but thinner at the parent. Consolidated cash plus undrawn revolvers was USD 3,620 million; the parent's share was USD 2,442 million (cash USD 1,973 million including restricted cash, plus USD 469 million undrawn) [CP-1]. The USD 643 million 2027 notes will be redeemed from cash on November 30, 2026, which reduces parent liquidity to about USD 1,799 million pro forma [CP-1, calculation below]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. The maturity wall starts in 2028. Debt maturing is USD 15 million in the remainder of 2026, USD 701 million in 2027, USD 3,766 million in 2028, USD 1,667 million in 2029, USD 4,123 million in 2030 and USD 3,896 million in 2031, with USD 6,000 million thereafter [CP-1]. The parent's 2028 maturities of USD 2,326 million exceed its pro forma liquidity of about USD 1,799 million, so repayment relies on cash generation or refinancing; the revolver also has an earlier-maturity trigger tied to indebtedness above USD 1,000 million [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 5. Earnings quality is price-led and concentrated. Salix revenue rose USD 343 million in nine months 2026 on price of USD 504 million, partly offset by volumes down USD 173 million, and Salix is about 27% of revenue but about 47% of segment profit [CP-1A]. Xifaxan is about 85% of Salix, faces a negotiated Medicare price from January 1, 2027 and expected generics in 2028, and the company impaired Salix goodwill by USD 1,426 million in January 2026 after failed Phase 3 trials [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the concentration shares are derived.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 6. Cash interest absorbs a large share of earnings. FY2025 cash interest was USD 1,810 million against derived EBITDA before goodwill impairments of USD 3,276 million, about 55% of it and a cover of 1.81x, and the pack gives no interim cash interest [CP-1]. Premium accounting makes P&L interest lower than cash interest, so cover on a P&L basis (2.53x LTM Q3 2026) is flattered [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact for inputs; Analyst Interpretation on direction.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 7. Structure matters as much as leverage. The 2025 first-lien debt at 126NumberCo holds a lien on 211,963,893 Bausch + Lomb shares, and sales proceeds must prepay it pro rata with the 2032 notes; other secured and unsecured notes rank structurally behind, and Bausch + Lomb's earnings and net debt are outside the covenant [CP-1A]. Legal capacity and exchange terms cannot be tested without the debt documents. [Documentary Fact.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 8. Governance evidence is mixed rather than adverse. No dividends and a USD 50 million buyback authorised, a cash repurchase of near-par unsecured notes in 2025 and extended maturities weigh against overlapping leadership of two listed entities and unresolved terms of exchanges [CP-1A]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings recovery with deleveraging. Derived LTM EBITDA before goodwill impairments rose from USD 3,276 million (FY2025) to USD 3,918 million (LTM Q3 2026) while principal debt stayed near USD 20,200 million, lowering gross leverage by about one turn [CP-1]. This reduces default risk on a going-concern basis. [Analyst Interpretation.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing already done. The 2025 refinancing and the December 2025 exchange extended about USD 6,870 million and USD 1,600 million of maturities to 2030 through 2032, so only USD 716 million falls due before 2028 on a consolidated basis, and USD 643 million of that is to be redeemed from cash [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact for the transactions; the 716 sum is derived.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash and parent deleveraging. Cash of USD 2,485 million and parent net debt down USD 521 million in Q3 2026 show cash generation reaching the parent group [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant exposure is limited and stated compliant. The revolver has two maintenance tests, and the company states compliance at September 30, 2026 [CP-1]. [Documentary Fact; the headroom is Not supplied.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Diversification outside Salix. International, Solta Medical and Bausch + Lomb grew in nine months 2026, and Bausch + Lomb produced about 27% of segment profit [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; the share is derived.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No shareholder leakage. No dividends in FY2025, FY2024 or FY2023, and restrictions in the debt documents [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Product concentration with dated erosion. Salix and Xifaxan dominate segment profit, and the negotiated price and generic entry are dated [CP-1A]. Mechanic: price-led growth meets a price cap, then volume loss. Implication: lower cash available for 2028 refinancing. [Documentary Fact for the dates; Analyst Interpretation on the effect.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - High leverage and modest cash cover. 5.15x gross leverage and 1.81x FY2025 cash interest cover leave limited tolerance for a profit decline [CP-1]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Large 2028 to 2031 maturities, USD 13,452 million in total, with USD 8,422 million of it at the parent [CP-1, calculation below]. [Analyst Interpretation.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Structural subordination and a separate Bausch + Lomb silo. Value in the Bausch + Lomb stake serves the 2025 first-lien debt first, and its cash is generally trapped [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weak credit ratings: Moody's Caa2 and S&P B- corporate, with a negative outlook at S&P and Rating Watch Evolving at Fitch [CP-1, CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Litigation and regulatory exposure: antitrust class actions on the Xifaxan settlement, a Luxembourg tax assessment with no reserve, an FDA warning letter at a Bausch + Lomb plant, and talc claims backed by an indemnity from Johnson & Johnson whose performance the pack does not test [CP-1A]. [Documentary Fact; amounts of exposure are Not supplied.]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Opaque adjusted measures. Adjusted EBITDA and adjusted cash flow are management-defined, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is missing, so no adjusted LTM leverage exists [CP-0, CP-1]. [Insufficient Information.]
